- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk reversal or market panic.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise after spike to 3–4% max.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) prices — apply 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment for final 10 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.8 to -0.6 in 2–3 days), model misreads momentum — use sentiment-weighted average of 2–3 prior days to anchor forecast.
